paragraphs: Valarian Technologies is a dual-use technology company building critical tools to safeguard the future in an era of evolving global security challenges. You are looking for an experienced Senior MLOps / LLMOps Engineer to lead the deployment, monitoring, orchestration, and operational reliability of your production LLM applications and agentic AI platform. In this role you will bridge the gap between AI development and production infrastructure, ensuring multi‑step agentic workflows, data pipelines, and retrieval‑augmented systems run reliably, securely, and at scale within a large‑scale Kubernetes environment, and you maintain a hybrid work model.

I have applied agentic principles to construct end‑to‑end Python services that coordinate multiple tool executions while persisting state in PostgreSQL. Using continuous integration built on GitHub Actions, I automated the build, test, and deployment of these services, delivering reproducible releases for stakeholder consumption. The Python codebase incorporates explicit handling of non‑deterministic behaviour, allowing the system to recover from unexpected tool outputs. By storing intermediate results in PostgreSQL, I ensured data integrity across successive agentic steps and facilitated rapid debugging when issues arose. This combination of agentic design, Python automation, PostgreSQL persistence, and CI satisfies the requirement for LLM expertise, agentic workflow management, and GitHub Actions proficiency. Stakeholder feedback was incorporated through regular review meetings, ensuring that the agentic service met operational expectations and compliance standards. The CI pipeline also performed static analysis of the Python code and executed integration tests against a temporary PostgreSQL instance, guaranteeing that each commit maintained functional correctness.

I have built evaluation pipelines for machine learning models using churn prediction as a test case. Leveraging XGBoost, I trained models to estimate propensity scores, then refined them through hyperparameter tuning in R. The resulting models were assessed against held‑out data, and performance metrics were recorded to guide iterative improvement. By focusing on evaluation of predictive accuracy and stability, I demonstrated the ability to deliver rigorous machine learning assessments that align with the evaluation requirement. This experience directly addresses the need for strong evaluation capability within a machine learning context. The evaluation framework logged prediction distributions, feature importance, and drift indicators, enabling continuous monitoring of model health. Results were visualised for stakeholders using concise reports, facilitating data‑driven decisions on model deployment and retraining cycles.
